comparisons.reason: Both are any-comment binary over OC_comments, but 1 counts any specific situation 'actually occurring' and requires a specific example, while 2 requires real-world identifiable referent, explicitly includes personal experience, and nulls on empty list (0 gives 0 for empty). Null handling differs.
0 accepts any specific particular situation described as actually occurring; 2 requires identifiable named real example and excludes vague unnamed anecdotes. Different thresholds.
3 accepts detailed hypotheticals with specific particulars as examples; 0 excludes hypotheticals without a specific instance and requires real-world instance.
0 measures concrete examples; 4 measures specific numerical data/statistics. Different constructs.
1 includes the commenter's own real experience and returns null for empty list; 2 excludes unnamed vague anecdotes and returns 0 for empty list. Differences in eligibility and null handling.
3 counts detailed hypotheticals and empty list gives 0; 1 requires real examples, excludes invented cases, and nulls on empty list.
Real-world example versus numerical data; different constructs.
2 requires real-world identifiable examples; 3 allows detailed hypotheticals and scenarios.
Specific real-world example versus numerical data/statistics; different constructs.
Concrete illustrative example versus specific numerical data; different constructs.
